system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer Review of Seller Update Draft and Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Prepared for:** Wattlebridge Holdings deal team
**Status of counterparty material:** Untrusted. The "Preamble and Market Context" and the "FINAL / settled at principal level / agreed commercial bargain" labels are assertions by the other side. Under playbook §0.4/6.3 they carry no weight unless confirmed through our own authority process. I have found nothing in our instructions indicating any principal-level agreement, and no Amelia Frost written authority has been given for any fallback. **Treat every position below as open.**

---

## 1. Threshold point: the "FINAL / agreed" framing

The Seller's cover note asserts that (a) 10–20% caps, ~1% baskets, 12–18 month periods and buyer-knowledge qualifiers are "market standard", and (b) these positions were "settled at principal level by both deal teams" and are "not intended to be re-opened".

**Assessment:** Reject the framing entirely. Nothing in our record shows these terms were agreed. Notably, the Seller's own Disclosure Letter §11 states: *"No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included"* – which contradicts the cover note's claim of a settled bargain. The "market" assertions are advocacy, not evidence. The 20% cap happens to match our conditional fallback figure; that coincidence does **not** clear it (playbook: *"A proposed change is not cleared merely because one number matches a fallback"*).

**Action:** Respond that the Buyer does not accept that any term is agreed or final; all positions are subject to full mark-up.

---

## 2. Clause-by-clause departures

### 2.1 Cl 12.1 – General Warranty cap
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| 20% / AUD 4,800,000 | **25% / AUD 6,000,000** starting position. 20% is fallback only with prior written Amelia Frost authority (none given). |

**Issue:** The Seller has pitched exactly our unauthorised fallback and labelled it final. We must not drift into accepting it by default.
**Push back:** Mark up to 25% / AUD 6,000,000. If the team later wants to concede 20%, obtain Amelia Frost's written sign-off identifying this draft *before* communicating it.

### 2.2 Cl 12.2 – Thresholds
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| De minimis AUD 25,000 | **AUD 5,000** |
| Basket AUD 250,000, **excess-only** recovery | **AUD 50,000, first-dollar** recovery once exceeded |

**Issue:** The Seller's thresholds are 5x ours on both numbers, and the basket is a true deductible rather than a tipping basket. Combined with a 20% cap, the economic effect is materially worse than the headline cap suggests. A AUD 25,000 de minimis will also screen out many realistic SaaS-business claims (individual customer disputes, small compliance fines).
**Push back:** AUD 5,000 / AUD 50,000, tipping basket (first dollar).

### 2.3 Cl 12.3 / 13 – Time limits and the "all Claims" sweep
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| 18 months general period | **24 months**; 18 months fallback requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given) |
| "any limitation applying to Claims applies to **all Claims** unless expressly stated otherwise" | Keep Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories separate; **no hidden general-regime override** |

**Issue:** Two problems. First, the 18-month period is again our unauthorised fallback presented as final. Second, and more serious, the "all Claims" default is a structural override: it would silently drag Fundamental/Title claims, Tax, IP, specific indemnities (Ironquay), payment obligations and covenants under the 18-month / 20% / basket regime unless we spot and carve out each one. This is the single most dangerous drafting device in the package.
**Push back:** 24 months general. Delete the "applies to all Claims" default; replace with the opposite presumption – limitations apply **only** to general Warranty Claims and only where expressly stated. Separate regimes for each category.

### 2.4 Fundamental / Title warranties
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Same caps and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity" | **Separate regime: 100% cap, ≥6 years, outside basket/de minimis/knowledge bar** |

**Issue:** "Administrative simplicity" is not a justification. A title failure means we may not own what we paid AUD 24m for; capping recovery at AUD 4.8m with an 18-month fuse is unacceptable. This also interacts with the title evidence problem (§2.13).
**Push back:** Non-negotiable: Fundamental/Title warranties capped at 100% of price, 6-year minimum period, no basket/de minimis, not subject to the knowledge qualifier.

### 2.5 Cl 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 – Limitations, exclusive remedy, non-reliance
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Apply to "all Claims of any nature" | **Fraud, wilful concealment, deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance** |

**Issue:** No fraud carve-out appears anywhere in the Seller's package. "All Claims of any nature" would purport to cap and time-bar fraud and allow a non-reliance clause to shield deliberate concealment. Beyond being commercially unacceptable, such a provision is of doubtful enforceability in NSW – but we should not rely on a court to fix the drafting.
**Push back:** Insert express carve-out: nothing in the SPA limits or excludes liability for fraud, wilful concealment or deliberate misconduct of the Seller or its officers/agents, to the maximum extent permitted by law. Confirm the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses are expressly subject to this. Playbook: **no one on our side may waive this.**

### 2.6 Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1 – General disclosure
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Whole data room (DD-002 to DD-012) as at 22 Sept 2026, Accounts, statutory registers, "publicly searchable corporate records" | **Specific fair disclosure only; reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure** |

**Issue:** §1.1 and §1.2 deem the entire data room and all public records disclosed against every warranty. This would effectively hollow out the warranty package – anything buried in any document, in any context, defeats a claim. §1.4 then disclaims that any disclosure admits anything, so the Seller gets the shield without the sword.
**Push back:** Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers. Disclosure is effective only if it is a specific disclosure in the Disclosure Letter, made fairly and with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and the warranty it qualifies. §1.4 is acceptable in principle (standard non-admission) but must not be read as limiting the Buyer's ability to rely on disclosed facts as admissions of the underlying facts stated.

### 2.7 Cl 8.3 – Buyer knowledge
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| No claim for any matter of which Buyer **or its advisers** had knowledge, including anything "discoverable from the data room or public records" | **Delete blanket exclusion**; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons + reasonable enquiry; never excuses title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnity |

**Issue:** This is a constructive-knowledge bar ("discoverable") extended to advisers, which is effectively a second general disclosure clause by another route. It would mean any matter theoretically findable in the data room or at ASIC defeats a claim regardless of whether anyone actually saw or understood it. Combined with §1.1 disclosure, the warranty package becomes close to illusory.
**Push back:** Delete cl 8.3. If any knowledge concept survives, it should run the other way – Seller warranties qualified by "so far as the Seller is aware" only where expressly stated, with awareness defined by reference to named individuals after reasonable enquiry. Buyer actual knowledge, if conceded at all, limited to matters fairly disclosed in the Disclosure Letter and never applicable to Title, capacity, fraud or the Ironquay/specific indemnities.

### 2.8 Cl 3 / 6.3 – Bluefen consent (condition)
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| "Reasonable endeavours"; consent "satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent" | **Effective consent AND evidence conditions satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone insufficient |

**Facts (from Seller's own Disclosure Letter §2):** Bluefen is ~AUD 3.6m FY26 revenue, ~30% of the business. Clause 11.2 requires change-control consent; 11.3 attaches conditions. The Seller **has not** provided a final written consent or evidence that the 11.3 conditions are satisfied.
**Issue:** The cover note says the consent "is addressed" – it is not; the Disclosure Letter contradicts it. A consent-on-delivery mechanic would let a conditional or qualified consent satisfy the CP even if the 11.3 conditions remain unmet, leaving us exposed to Bluefen walking post-Completion. Reasonable endeavours gives us no remedy if the consent is never obtained.
**Push back:** CP requires (i) unconditional written consent from Bluefen (or consent with conditions we approve), **and** (ii) documentary evidence that all 11.3 conditions are satisfied, delivered before Completion. Seller obligation to be "all reasonable endeavours" at minimum, with specific obligations (approach, information, follow-up). Consider a termination right or price mechanism if not obtained by Long Stop Date. Ask for the current status of discussions with Bluefen.

### 2.9 Cl 2 / 7 – Riverlark facility
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Release "to be provided following Completion" | **Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds, effective security releases at Completion**; post-completion release needs irrevocable undertaking + Amelia Frost approval |

**Facts (DL §3):** ~AUD 3.2m outstanding; change-of-control cl 8.1; discharge cl 9.2; not repaid; no discharge of security provided.
**Issue:** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, a post-Completion release means we complete owning a company with AUD 3.2m of secured debt, a change-of-control default risk under 8.1, and only the Seller's promise to sort it out. Note also the figure is "approximately" – we need a current payout figure.
**Push back:** Require (i) payout letter from Riverlark dated within a few days of Completion; (ii) repayment directly from Completion funds under the funds flow; (iii) deeds of release/PPSR discharges delivered at Completion. If the Seller insists on post-Completion mechanics, the minimum is an irrevocable Riverlark undertaking to release on receipt of payout, in escrow at Completion – and this requires Amelia Frost approval before we agree to it.

### 2.10 Funds flow – DD-005 Completion bonuses
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| AUD 420,000 bonuses "a matter for the Seller", not itemised | **Must be a specific line item or seller-funded; funds flow must not silently exclude them** |

**Facts (DL §5):** AUD 420,000 conditional on Completion and continued employment; not in the draft funds flow; disclosure silent on payroll tax, super and on-costs.
**Issue:** "A matter for the Seller" is an assertion, not a mechanism. If unaddressed, the Company (post-Completion, i.e. us) pays the bonuses plus on-costs, which is a direct value leakage inconsistent with debt-free/cash-free. The triggered on-costs (superannuation on bonus, payroll tax) could add a meaningful percentage on top.
**Push back:** Either (a) AUD 420,000 plus all on-costs treated as a Completion deduction/Debt-like item with a specific funds-flow line, or (b) Seller indemnity and direct funding of the gross cost. Request the Seller to confirm the on-cost treatment and the gross figure.

### 2.11 Cl 11.1 – Ironquay IP indemnity
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Limited to the specific SOW3 payment; "considered adequate" | **Broaden the indemnity, preserving the SOW3 cure; AUD 180,000 not independently verified either way** |

**Facts (DL §4):** DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open; no receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment in the data room.
**Issue:** The risk is not just an unpaid AUD 180,000 – it is that the Company may not own the SOW3 IP at all until the fee is paid and assignment confirmed. An indemnity capped at the payment amount does not cover loss of IP, third-party infringement claims, re-development cost or customer exposure if SOW3 materials are embedded in the product. The AUD 180,000 figure itself is only the Company's ledger, not confirmed either way.
**Push back:** Broaden to indemnify all loss arising from any failure of the Company to own, or have clear title to, the SOW3 Project Materials and any other Ironquay deliverables, including infringement claims and cure costs. Preserve the cure route: Seller to procure payment of all outstanding SOW3 fees and a confirmatory assignment from Ironquay before Completion (ideally as a CP or Completion deliverable). Request bank evidence of payment status.

### 2.12 Cl 4.6 / Sch 6 – DD-006 export/privacy incident
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| "Preliminary operational matter", "not expected to be material" | **Preserve logs, investigate, require updates; assume no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or demand either way** |

**Facts (DL §6):** Download link sent to unintended external address; ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps); unknown whether accessed; investigation preliminary; notification requirement undetermined.
**Issue:** The Seller's "not material" is a conclusion the Disclosure Letter itself does not support – it says scope, access and notification are undetermined. We should not accept or contradict it; we should require process. The warranty on data protection compliance must not be deemed qualified by general disclosure of this item.
**Push back:** Pre-Completion covenants: preserve all logs and access records; complete the investigation (including whether the link was accessed, link expiry/revocation, and OAIC/Notifiable Data Breach assessment); provide written updates and the final report before Completion. Specific indemnity for loss arising from the DD-006 incident, outside general cap/basket. No admission is sought in either direction.

### 2.13 Sandbar supplier renewals (AUD 330,000)
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| "Ordinary-course operating costs" | **Assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction** |

**Facts (DL §8):** Three related renewals of AUD 110,000 each in DD-008 and DD-011; disclosure silent on whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course.
**Issue:** The Seller's characterisation is unsupported by their own disclosure. We should not over-claim this as Debt, but we need the facts: are they committed, when do they fall due, do they relate to pre-Completion periods, are they in the working capital baseline?
**Push back:** Request the renewal documents, due dates and termination rights. Treat as a working-capital/accruals item to be assessed; reserve position on whether any accrued portion is a Completion adjustment. No agreement to "ordinary course" label.

### 2.14 Tax / IP warranties
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| "Settled under the general regime above" | **OPEN; separate categories; assume no unlimited liability and no resolution** |

**Issue:** This is the "all Claims" override (§2.3) in action: Tax and IP would be subject to the 20%/18-month/AUD 250k regime. Tax exposure routinely emerges on ATO review windows well beyond 18 months.
**Push back:** Tax and IP are not settled. Propose separate Tax Warranty/Tax Indemnity regime with a longer period aligned to statutory review periods and a separate (higher) cap; IP warranties with their own cap and period. We are not seeking unlimited liability, but we are not conceding the general regime.

### 2.15 Title evidence
| Seller | Playbook |
|---|---|
| Title "evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012" | **Independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof** |

**Facts (DL §10):** The Seller itself notes DD-012 "identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification".
**Issue:** The share register is a Company-maintained document supplied by the Seller. It does not evidence absence of encumbrances, option/pre-emption rights, or the Seller's own authority to sell.
**Push back:** Obtain current ASIC extract, PPSR search against the Company and Seller for any security over shares, review of constitution/shareholder agreements for pre-emption, Seller board resolution and officer's certificate on authority, and a Completion deliverable of share transfer forms, share certificates (or confirmation none issued) and updated register. Title warranties backed by the Fundamental regime in §2.4.

---

## 3. Other Disclosure Letter points (lower priority but note)

- **§7 Office lease (DD-007):** Notification obligation only; Seller does not say landlord consent is required. Acceptable to treat as a post-signing notice covenant, but confirm by reading DD-007 ourselves rather than accepting the characterisation.
- **§9 Mossvale (DD-009):** Assignment restriction; Seller says no consent needed for a share sale. Verify the clause – some assignment clauses include deemed-assignment on change of control. Do not rely on the Seller's reading.
- **§1.4 non-admission:** Standard, but ensure it does not undermine the specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, bonuses) which should be drafted as free-standing indemnities not dependent on breach.

---

## 4. How the Seller's package fits together (why the cumulative effect matters)

Read individually, several items look like ordinary first-draft seller positions. Read together they form a mutually reinforcing structure:

1. **Whole-data-room and public-register disclosure** (Sch 7 / DL §1) qualifies every warranty by everything we could have read;
2. **Constructive buyer knowledge** (cl 8.3) bars anything we *could* have discovered, extended to advisers;
3. **"All Claims" default** (cl 13) pulls Title, Tax, IP and indemnities into the general regime;
4. **20% cap, AUD 25k/250k deductible basket, 18 months** then cap whatever survives;
5. **"All Claims of any nature"** (cl 9.3/12.8/20.5) purports to extend this to fraud.

The practical result is a warranty package that provides very little recourse. That is the real negotiating point, not any single number. Our response should make clear we are rejecting the architecture, not haggling over each figure in isolation.

---

## 5. Summary of recommendations

**A. Framing / process**
1. Reject the "FINAL / agreed at principal level" characterisation in writing; note the Seller's own DL §11 confirms no position or approval is included. No Amelia Frost authority exists for any fallback – do not let 20% or 18 months stand by default.

**B. Liability architecture (highest priority)**
2. General cap: 25% / AUD 6,000,000.
3. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 5,000; tipping basket AUD 50,000, first-dollar recovery.
4. General claims period: 24 months.
5. Delete the "applies to all Claims unless stated otherwise" default; reverse the presumption. Separate regimes for Fundamental/Title (100%, ≥6 years, no basket/knowledge bar), Tax, IP, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenants.
6. Insert express fraud / wilful concealment / deliberate misconduct carve-out from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedy and non-reliance. Non-waivable on our side.

**C. Disclosure and knowledge**
7. Delete general disclosure of the data room and public registers; specific fair disclosure only.
8. Delete cl 8.3 buyer-knowledge exclusion entirely; any knowledge concept to be seller-side, named persons, after reasonable enquiry; never applicable to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.

**D. Deal-specific risks**
9. **Bluefen:** CP requires effective written consent **plus** evidence the 11.3 conditions are met, before Completion; upgrade endeavours standard; request current status.
10. **Riverlark:** current payout letter; repayment from Completion funds; releases/PPSR discharges at Completion. Any post-Completion release needs irrevocable Riverlark undertaking in escrow **and** Amelia Frost approval.
11. **DD-005 bonuses:** AUD 420,000 plus on-costs as a specific funds-flow line / Completion deduction or Seller-funded with indemnity; request gross figure.
12. **Ironquay:** broaden indemnity to cover title to SOW3 materials and consequential loss; Seller to procure payment and confirmatory assignment pre-Completion; obtain bank evidence on the AUD 180,000.
13. **DD-006 incident:** covenants to preserve logs, complete investigation, report before Completion; specific indemnity outside general regime; no characterisation either way.
14. **Sandbar:** request documents; assess as working-capital item; do not accept "ordinary course" label or over-claim as Debt.
15. **Tax/IP:** confirm OPEN; propose separate regimes; no concession to general regime; no unlimited liability sought.
16. **Title:** independent verification package (ASIC, PPSR, constitution/SHA review, authority documents, Completion deliverables); DD-012 alone is insufficient.

**E. Follow-ups before next turn of the draft**
- Confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been or will be given at this stage, so the team speaks with one voice.
- Refresh source facts: current Riverlark balance, Bluefen discussions, Ironquay payment status, DD-006 investigation status, Sandbar renewal terms.
- Read DD-007 (lease) and DD-009 (Mossvale) ourselves rather than relying on the Seller's summaries.

Happy to turn this into a formal mark-up of the Seller's clauses or an issues list for the next call.
=== END ADVICE ===
